title: Seaworth — business context library
purpose: Structured, sourced business context for Seaworth: who gets attacked at sea, where, what it costs, and who actually owns and rents the ships. Every dataset is plain JSON so it can be lifted into an application without rewriting.

conventions.join_key: IMO number for vessels. Never ship name — names change, IMO numbers do not.
conventions.ids: Lowercase kebab-case, stable across versions. Cross-dataset references use <dataset>_id fields.
conventions.dates: ISO 8601. Periods as YYYY, YYYY-Qn, or YYYY-H1.
conventions.provenance: Every quantitative record carries source_ids into sources.json.
conventions.confidence: high — read from the publishing body. medium — reported by a credible secondary outlet. low — aggregator or unverified; do not quote externally without checking.
conventions.shelf_life: Piracy data goes stale in months, not years. The Somali reading changed completely between the 2025 annual reports and the H1 2026 half-years. Check the date on every record before relying on it.
conventions.no_interpretation: Records carry facts and sources. Analysis, inference and framing are deliberately absent; add them where they are used, not here.
conventions.flags: Flag images come from flagsapi.com by ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, held in flag_iso fields. Null where the source does not name a flag.
conventions.map: Coordinates are [lat, lon] decimal degrees. The map projects equirectangular into a 2000x1000 box; see tools/build-world-path.py.
conventions.dating: Every source and company record carries a retrieved date — when this library last read it. Dataset files carry a top-level retrieved date. A figure without a date is not usable; a figure with an old date is a re-check, not a fact.
